candidate_profile.description: The candidate correctly identifies private label mix as the key profitability lever and can broadly validate management's plan, though the synthesis and risk framing are solid rather than outstanding.
behaviour_rules: Start with a clear recap and frame the case as a profitability issue driven by revenue mix and margins.
Recognize that the issue is pervasive across stores and that store closures or short-term expansion are not the immediate answer.
Use Exhibit #1 to infer that private label growth historically supported profit growth.
Understand that private label has a materially higher gross margin than national brands.
Correctly compute or approximately explain that a 3 percentage point penetration shift on $60B revenue produces enough profit improvement to meet the target after taxes.
Ask for the tax rate or otherwise recognize that after-tax profit is the relevant metric.
Recommend proceeding with the private label focus, while also calling for some validation of the assumptions.

expected_issues: Gets to the right answer, but may not make the private-label-to-profit linkage especially sharp at first.
Math may be correct but not especially elegant or executive-ready.
Recommendation can be somewhat light on one-time costs, supplier effects, and pilot design.
expected_feedback_points: Good diagnosis that private label mix is a major profitability lever.
Good validation that management's hypothesis meets the profit goal.
Good recognition that taxes matter in the final impact estimate.
Reasonable recommendation to pursue private label, with some validation work before rollout.
